verses.1:1: Words of the Assembler, son of David, king of Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.1:2: "Futility of futilities," said the Assembler, "futility of futilities; all things are futility."
verses.1:3: What advantage does a man have in all his toil at which he toils under the sun?
verses.1:4: A generation goes and a generation comes, and the earth stands forever.
verses.1:5: And the sun rises, and the sun sets, and draws to its place;
verses.1:6: rising there, it goes toward the south and circles toward the north; circling, it circles; the wind goes, and to its circuits the wind returns.
verses.1:7: All the streams go into the sea, and the sea will not be filled; to the place the streams go, there they return to go.
verses.1:8: All words are wearisome; a man will not be able to speak, and an eye will not be satisfied with seeing, and an ear will not be filled from hearing.
verses.1:9: What is that which has come to be? It is that which will come to be. And what is that which has been done? It is that which will be done. And there is nothing fresh under the sun.
verses.1:10: Whoever speaks and says, "See, this is new"—it has already come to be in the ages that were before us.
verses.1:11: There is no remembrance of the first ones, and indeed of the last ones who have come to be; there will be no remembrance of them among those who will come to be at the last.
verses.1:12: I, the Assembler, became king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.1:13: And I gave my heart to seek out and to examine in wisdom concerning all the things that happen under heaven; for God has given an evil preoccupation to the sons of men to be preoccupied with it.
verses.1:14: I saw all the works that have been done under the sun, and look, all things are futility and a choice of spirit.
verses.1:15: What is crooked will not be able to be put in order, and a deficiency will not be able to be counted.
verses.1:16: I spoke in my heart, saying, "Look, I have grown great and have added wisdom beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem."
verses.1:17: And my heart saw much—wisdom and knowledge—and I gave my heart to know wisdom and knowledge; parables and understanding I came to know. For this too is a choice of spirit,
verses.1:18: because in an abundance of wisdom is an abundance of knowledge, and the one who adds knowledge will add pain.
verses.2:1: I said in my heart, "Come now, I will test you with gladness, and look upon good." And look, this too is futility.
verses.2:2: To laughter I said, "Madness," and to gladness, "What is this you are doing?"
verses.2:3: And I examined whether my heart would draw my flesh like wine—and my heart guided in wisdom—and to take hold of gladness, until I should see what is the good for the sons of men that they will do under the sun for the number of the days of their life.
verses.2:4: I made my work great; I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself;
verses.2:5: I made gardens and parks for myself, and I planted in them every fruit tree;
verses.2:6: I made pools of water for myself, to water from them a sprouting forest;
verses.2:7: I acquired male servants and female servants, and homeborn ones became mine; and also a great possession of herd and flock became mine, beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem;
verses.2:8: I gathered for myself both silver and gold, and treasures of kings and of the regions; I provided for myself male singers and female singers, delights of the sons of men, a male cupbearer and female cupbearers.
verses.2:9: And I grew great and increased beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem; and indeed my wisdom stood with me.
verses.2:10: And everything that my eyes asked for I did not withhold from them; I did not keep my heart back from all my gladness, for my heart was glad in all my toil; and this became my portion from all my toil.
verses.2:11: And I looked upon all my works that my hands had made, and upon the toil at which I toiled to do so, and look, all things are futility and a choice of spirit, and there is no advantage under the sun.
verses.2:12: And I looked to see wisdom and madness and folly; for who is the man who will come after the counsel? All the things that he did to it.
verses.2:13: And I saw that there is an advantage to wisdom over folly, like the advantage of light over darkness.
verses.2:14: The wise man's eyes are in his head, and the fool walks in darkness. And I too came to know that one fate will meet all of them.
verses.2:15: And I said in my heart, "As is the fate of the fool, even to me, it will meet me; and why did I become wise?" I spoke excessively in my heart that this too is futility, because the fool speaks out of excess.
verses.2:16: For there is no remembrance of the wise man with the fool forever, since already in the coming days all things have been forgotten; and how will the wise man die with the fool?
verses.2:17: And I hated life, because the work that has been done under the sun was evil to me, for everything is futility and a choice of spirit.
verses.2:18: And I hated all my toil at which I labor under the sun, because I leave it to the man who comes after me.
verses.2:19: And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? And will he have authority over all my toil at which I toiled and acted wisely under the sun? This too is futility.
verses.2:20: And I turned to renounce my heart concerning all my toil at which I toiled under the sun,
verses.2:21: because there is a man whose toil is in wisdom and in knowledge and in prowess, and to a man who did not toil in it he will give his portion; this too is futility and a great evil.
verses.2:22: For it happens to man in all his toil and in the choice of his heart at which he toils under the sun.
verses.2:23: For all his days are of pains, and his preoccupation is of anger; even at night his heart does not sleep. This too is futility.
verses.2:24: There is no good for a man, that he should eat and that he should drink and that he should show his soul good in his toil; this too I saw, that it is from the hand of God.
verses.2:25: For who will eat and who will drink apart from Him?
verses.2:26: For to the man who is good before His face He has given wisdom and knowledge and gladness; and to the one who sins He has given the preoccupation of adding and of gathering, to give to the one who is good before the face of God. For this too is futility and a choice of spirit.
verses.3:1: For all things there is a time, and a season for every matter under heaven.
verses.3:2: A season to give birth and a season to die, a season to plant and a season to uproot what has been planted,
verses.3:3: a season to kill and a season to heal, a season to tear down and a season to build,
verses.3:4: a season to weep and a season to laugh, a season to mourn and a season to dance,
verses.3:5: a season to throw stones and a season to gather stones, a season to embrace and a season to keep far from embracing,
verses.3:6: a season to seek and a season to lose, a season to keep and a season to cast away,
verses.3:7: a season to tear and a season to sew, a season to keep silent and a season to speak,
verses.3:8: a season to love and a season to hate, a season of war and a season of peace.
verses.3:9: What is the advantage of the worker in the things at which he toils?
verses.3:10: I saw all the preoccupation that God has given to the sons of men to be preoccupied with it.
verses.3:11: Everything that He has made is beautiful in its season; He has also put all eternity in their heart, so that man may not find the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
verses.3:12: I came to know that there is no good among them, except to be glad and to do good in his life;
verses.3:13: and also, every man who will eat and drink and see good in all his toil—it is a gift of God.
verses.3:14: I came to know that all things that God has done, they will be forever; there is no adding to it, and there is no taking away from it; and God has done so, that they may fear before His face.
verses.3:15: What has come to be already is, and all things that are to come to be have already come to be; and God will seek the one who is pursued.
verses.3:16: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment—there was the ungodly one; and the place of the righteous one—there was the godly one.
verses.3:17: And I said in my heart, "Both the righteous and the ungodly God will judge, for there is a season for every matter and for every work."
verses.3:18: And I said in my heart concerning the speech of the sons of man, that God will judge them, and to show that they themselves are beasts.
verses.3:19: And indeed for them, is there not a fate of the sons of man and a fate of the beast? One fate belongs to them: as is the death of the one, so is the death of the other, and there is one spirit for all of them. And what advantage has man over the beast? Nothing, for everything is futility.
verses.3:20: All things go to one place; all things came to be from the dust, and all things will return to the dust.
verses.3:21: And who knows the spirit of the sons of man, whether it goes upward? And the spirit of the beast, whether it goes downward into the earth?
verses.3:22: And I saw that there is no good, except that a man should be glad in his works, for that is his portion; for who will bring him to see whatever may come to be after him?
verses.4:1: And I turned back and saw all the oppressions that take place under the sun; look, the tear of those who are oppressed, and there is no one comforting them; and from the hand of those who oppress them there is power, and there is no one comforting them.
verses.4:2: And I praised all the dead who have already died more than the living, as many as are themselves living until now;
verses.4:3: and better than these two is the one who has not yet come into being, who has not seen all the evil work that has been done under the sun.
verses.4:4: And I saw all the toil and all the prowess of the work, that jealousy comes to a man from his companion; this too is futility and choice of spirit.
verses.4:5: The fool clasps his hands together and eats his own flesh.
verses.4:6: Better is a full handful of rest than two full handfuls of toil and choice of spirit.
verses.4:7: And I turned back and saw futility under the sun.
verses.4:8: There is one, and there is no second; indeed, he has neither son nor brother, and there is no end to all his toil, and even his eye is not satisfied with wealth. And for whom am I toiling and depriving my soul of goodness? This too is futility and an evil preoccupation.
verses.4:9: Two are better than one, who have a good reward in their toil;
verses.4:10: for if they fall, the one will lift up his partner; and woe to that single one when he falls and there is no second to lift him up.
verses.4:11: Moreover, if two lie down, then there is warmth for them; and how can the single one be warmed?
verses.4:12: And if one prevails, the two will stand against him, and the threefold cord will not quickly be torn apart.
verses.4:13: Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who no longer knows how to pay attention;
verses.4:14: for from the house of the prisoners he will come out to reign, because even in his kingdom he became poor.
verses.4:15: I saw all the living who walk under the sun with the second young man, who will stand in his place;
verses.4:16: there is no end to all the people, to all who were before them; yet even the later ones will not rejoice in him. For this too is futility and choice of spirit.
verses.4:17: Guard your foot whenever you go to the house of God, and be near to listen; better than the gift of fools is your sacrifice, for they are not aware of doing evil.
verses.5:1: Do not be hasty with your mouth, and do not let your heart hurry to bring out a word before the face of God; for God is in heaven above, and you are on the earth; therefore let your words be few.
verses.5:2: For a dream comes in an abundance of trial, and the voice of a fool in an abundance of words.
verses.5:3: When you vow a vow to God, do not delay to pay it. There is no pleasure in fools; you, therefore, pay whatever you vow.
verses.5:4: It is better for you not to vow than for you to vow and not pay.
verses.5:5: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before the face of God, "It is an oversight," so that God does not become angry at your voice and destroy the works of your hands.
verses.5:6: For in an abundance of dreams and futilities and many words—rather, as for you, fear God.
verses.5:7: If you see oppression of a poor person and robbery of justice and righteousness in a region, do not be amazed at the matter; a high one is over a high one to watch, and high ones are over them;
verses.5:8: and the advantage of the land; over all is a king of the cultivated field.
verses.5:9: One who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver; and who has loved yield in their abundance? This too is futility.
verses.5:10: In an abundance of goodness, those who eat it multiply; and what prowess is there for its owner? For it is a beginning for his eye to see.
verses.5:11: Sweet is the sleep of the servant, whether he eats little or much; but for the one who is filled with becoming rich, there is no one letting him sleep.
verses.5:12: There is a sickness that I saw under the sun: wealth guarded for its owner to his harm,
verses.5:13: and that wealth will perish in an evil preoccupation, and he fathered a son, and there is nothing in his hand;
verses.5:14: just as he came out from his mother's womb naked, he will return to go as he has come, and he will take nothing in his toil so that it may go in his hand.
verses.5:15: This too is an evil sickness: for just as he came, so also he will depart; and the advantage to him for which he toils is for the wind.
verses.5:16: Moreover, all his days are in darkness and in mourning and much anger and sickness and wrath.
verses.5:17: Look, I have seen a good thing that is fitting: to eat and to drink and to see goodness in all his toil in which he toils under the sun for the number of the days of his life that God has given him; for this is his portion.
verses.5:18: Moreover, every person to whom God has given wealth and possessions and granted authority over them, to eat from it and to take his share and to rejoice in his toil—this is a gift of God.
verses.5:19: For he will not remember other things during the days of his life, because God preoccupies him in the gladness of his heart.
verses.6:1: There is an evil that I saw under the sun, and it is great under mankind:
verses.6:2: a man to whom God will give wealth and possessions and honor, and he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he will desire; yet God will not grant him authority to eat from it, for a foreign man will eat it. This is futility and an evil sickness.
verses.6:3: If a man fathers a hundred and lives many years, and however abundant the days of his years will be, yet his soul will not be satisfied with the goodness, and he even had no burial, I said, "Better than him is the stillborn child";
verses.6:4: for it came in futility and goes in darkness, and in darkness its name will be covered,
verses.6:5: moreover, it did not see the sun, and it did not know; there is more rest for this one than for that one.
verses.6:6: And if he lived cycles of a thousand years, yet did not see goodness, does he not go to one place?
verses.6:7: All the toil of a person is for his mouth, and yet the soul will not be filled.
verses.6:8: For there is an advantage to the wise over the fool, because the poor person knows how to walk before life.
verses.6:9: Better is a sight of the eyes than what goes in the soul; this too is futility and choice of spirit.
verses.6:10: Whatever has come into being, its name has already been called, and it is known what a human being is, and he will not be able to contend in judgment with the one who is stronger than him;
verses.6:11: for there are many words that multiply futility.
verses.6:12: What advantage is there for a person? For who knows what is good for a person in life, during the number of the days of his life of futility? And he spent them in a shadow; for who will report to a person what will be after him under the sun?
verses.7:1: A name is better than good oil, and the day of death than the day of birth.
verses.7:2: It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of drinking, because this is the end of every man, and the living one will put good into his heart.
verses.7:3: Anger is better than laughter, because through badness of face it will be made good.
verses.7:4: The heart of the wise is in a house of mourning, and the heart of fools is in a house of gladness.
verses.7:5: It is better to hear the rebuke of a wise man than for a man to hear the song of fools.
verses.7:6: Like the sound of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of fools. Indeed, this also is futility.
verses.7:7: For oppression drives a wise man mad and destroys the heart of his nobility.
verses.7:8: The end of words is better than their beginning; one who is patient is better than one who is lofty in spirit.
verses.7:9: Do not be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger will rest in the bosom of fools.
verses.7:10: Do not say, "Why did it happen that the former days were better than these?" for it is not in wisdom that you asked about this.
verses.7:11: Wisdom is good with an inheritance, and an advantage for those who see the sun.
verses.7:12: For in its shadow wisdom is like the shadow of silver, and the advantage of the knowledge of wisdom will give life to the one who belongs to it.
verses.7:13: Look at the works of God, for who will be able to set in order the one whom God has made crooked?
verses.7:14: In a day of goodness live in good, and consider in a day of adversity. Look, God also made this in harmony with that concerning speech, so that man may find nothing after him.
verses.7:15: I saw all things in the days of my futility: there is a righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and there is an ungodly man remaining in his evil.
verses.7:16: Do not become greatly righteous, nor make yourself excessively wise, so that you may not be stunned.
verses.7:17: Do not be greatly ungodly, and do not become hard, so that you may not die when it is not your time.
verses.7:18: It is good that you hold fast to this, and from this also do not defile your hand, for all things will come forth for those who fear God.
verses.7:19: Wisdom will help the wise man more than ten rulers who are in the city.
verses.7:20: For there is no righteous man on the earth who will do good and will not sin.
verses.7:21: Also, do not set your heart on all the words that the ungodly will speak, so that you may not hear your servant cursing you;
verses.7:22: for very often he will treat you wickedly and many times he will afflict your heart, because in the same way you also cursed others.
verses.7:23: All these things I tested in wisdom. I said, "I will become wise," yet it was far removed from me.
verses.7:24: Far beyond what was, and a deep depth, who will find it?
verses.7:25: I myself turned about, and my heart, to know and to examine and to seek wisdom and a reckoning, and to know the foolishness of an ungodly man, and disturbance and madness.
verses.7:26: And I find her, and I will declare what is more bitter than death: the woman who is a snare, and her heart is dragnets, a bond on her hands. One who is good before the face of God will be delivered from her, and a sinner will be captured by her.
verses.7:27: Look, this I found, said the Assembler, one by one, to find reasoning,
verses.7:28: which my soul sought, and I did not find; and one man out of a thousand I found, but a woman among all these I did not find.
verses.7:29: Only look, this I found: that God made man upright, yet they themselves sought many reasonings. Who knows the wise? And who knows the interpretation of a word?
verses.8:1: A man's wisdom will illuminate his face, and one shameless in his face will be hated.
verses.8:2: Keep the mouth of a king, and concerning the word of an oath of God,
verses.8:3: do not be hasty; you will go from his presence; do not stand in an evil matter, for everything that he wills he will do,
verses.8:4: just as a king exercising authority; and who will say to him, "What are you doing?"
verses.8:5: The one who keeps a commandment will not know an evil thing, and the heart of a wise man knows a time of judgment.
verses.8:6: For to every matter there is a time and a judgment, because the knowledge of man is great upon him;
verses.8:7: for there is no one who knows what will be, for who will report to him how it will be?
verses.8:8: There is no man who has authority over the spirit to restrain the spirit, and there is no authority in the day of death, and there is no discharge in the day of war, and ungodliness will not deliver the one who belongs to it.
verses.8:9: And all of this I saw, and I gave my heart to every work that has been done under the sun, all the things in which man has exercised authority over man to harm him.
verses.8:10: And then I saw the ungodly brought into tombs, and from the holy place; and they went and were praised in the city, because they did so. Indeed, this also is futility.
verses.8:11: Because no contradiction is made quickly from those who do evil, therefore the heart of the sons of man within them is fully convinced to do evil.
verses.8:12: He who sinned did evil from then on and from their long duration; yet I also know that it is good for those who fear God, so that they may fear before His face.
verses.8:13: And it will not be good for the ungodly man, and he will not prolong days in a shadow, who does not fear before the face of God.
verses.8:14: There is a futility that has been done on the earth: that there are righteous people upon whom it comes like the work of the ungodly, and there are ungodly people to whom it comes like the work of the righteous. I said that this also is futility.
verses.8:15: And I praised gladness, because there is no good for man under the sun except to eat and to drink and to be glad; and this will accompany him in his toil for the days of his life, as many as God has given him under the sun.
verses.8:16: When I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see the preoccupation that has been done on the earth, for both by day and by night one does not see sleep with his eyes,
verses.8:17: then I saw all the works of God, that man will not be able to find the work that has been done under the sun. However much man may toil to seek, he will not find; and even however much a wise man may say he knows, he will not be able to find. For all of this I put to my heart, and with my heart I saw all of this:
verses.9:1: that the righteous and the wise and their deeds are in the hand of God; neither love nor hatred does man know; all things are before their face,
verses.9:2: futility in all things. There is one fate for the righteous and for the ungodly, for the good and for the bad, and for the clean and for the unclean, and for the one who sacrifices and for the one who does not sacrifice. As is the good man, so is the sinner; so is the one who swears, just as the one who fears the oath.
verses.9:3: This is an evil in everything done under the sun, that there is one fate for all. And also the heart of the sons of man is filled with evil, and madness is in their heart during their life, and after them, to the dead.
verses.9:4: For who is there who shares with all the living? There is hope, for the living dog itself is better than the dead lion.
verses.9:5: For the living will know that they will die, but the dead know nothing; and there is no longer a reward for them, for their memory has been forgotten.
verses.9:6: Indeed, their love, and their hatred, and their jealousy as well have already perished; and there is no longer a portion for them forever in everything that has been done under the sun.
verses.9:7: Come, eat your bread in gladness, and drink your wine with a good heart, for God has already been pleased with your works.
verses.9:8: At every time let your garments be white, and let oil not be lacking on your head.
verses.9:9: And see life with a wife whom you have loved all the days of the life of your futility that have been given to you under the sun. All are days of your vapor, for this is your portion in your life and in your toil at which you toil under the sun.
verses.9:10: All that your hand finds to do, do according to your strength, for there is no work or reasoning or knowledge or wisdom in Hades, where you are going.
verses.9:11: I turned and saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, and war is not to the mighty, and also bread is not to the wise man, nor wealth to the discerning, and also favor is not to those who know; for time and chance will meet all of them.
verses.9:12: For indeed, man also does not know his time: like the fish that are caught in an evil net, and like birds that are caught in a trap, like them the sons of man are trapped at an evil time, when it falls upon them suddenly.
verses.9:13: This also I saw as wisdom under the sun, and it is great to me:
verses.9:14: a small city, and few men in it; and a great king may come against it and surround it and build great siegeworks against it,
verses.9:15: and may find in it a poor wise man, and he himself may deliver the city by his wisdom, yet no one remembered that poor man.
verses.9:16: And I said, "Wisdom is better than strength," yet the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded.
verses.9:17: Words of the wise are heard in quietness more than the shout of rulers in follies.
verses.9:18: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner will destroy much goodness.
verses.10:1: Deadly flies will spoil a preparation, oil of sweet spice; the word of wisdom is more precious than the glory of great foolishness.
verses.10:2: The heart of a wise man is toward his right, and the heart of a fool is toward his left.
verses.10:3: And even when a fool walks on the road, his heart will be lacking, and all that he will consider is foolishness.
verses.10:4: If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, do not leave your place, for healing will put an end to great sins.
verses.10:5: There is an evil that I saw under the sun, like an unintentional error that proceeded from the presence of a ruler.
verses.10:6: The fool was set in great heights, and the rich will sit in a low place.
verses.10:7: I saw servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the ground.
verses.10:8: The one who digs a pit will fall into it, and a snake will bite one who tears down a fence.
verses.10:9: One who removes stones will be hurt by them; one who splits logs will be endangered by them.
verses.10:10: If the iron falls off, and he has troubled the face, then he will strengthen forces, and the advantage for the man is not wisdom.
verses.10:11: If a snake bites when there is no whispering, then there is no advantage for the charmer.
verses.10:12: The words of a wise man's mouth are grace, and the lips of a fool will drown him.
verses.10:13: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness, and his end is evil madness.
verses.10:14: And the fool multiplies words. A man does not know what has happened and what will be; what is after him, who will tell him?
verses.10:15: The toil of fools will afflict them—one who does not know how to go to a city.
verses.10:16: Woe to you, city, whose king is a youth, and your princes eat in the morning.
verses.10:17: Blessed are you, land, whose king is a son of free men, and your princes will eat at the proper time in strength and will not be put to shame.
verses.10:18: Through laziness the ceiling will sink low, and through idleness of hands the house will leak.
verses.10:19: For laughter they make bread, and wine and oil so that the living may rejoice, and all things will answer to the humbling of money.
verses.10:20: Even in your conscience do not curse a king, and in the inner rooms of your bedrooms do not curse a rich man; for a bird of the sky will carry away your voice, and the one with wings will report your word.
verses.11:1: Send out your bread upon the surface of the water, for in a multitude of days you will find it.
verses.11:2: Give a portion to seven, and even to eight, for you do not know what evil will be on the earth.
verses.11:3: If the clouds are filled with rain, they pour it out on the earth; and if a tree falls in the south or if in the north, in the place where the tree will fall, there it will be.
verses.11:4: One who observes the wind will not sow, and one who looks at the clouds will not harvest.
verses.11:5: In matters where there is no one who knows what the way of the spirit is, like bones in the womb of a pregnant woman, so you will not know the works of God, all that He will make, all things together.
verses.11:6: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not let your hand slacken, for you do not know which one will succeed, either this or that, or whether both alike are good.
verses.11:7: And sweet is the light, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.
verses.11:8: For even if a man lives many years, he will rejoice in all of them, and he will remember the days of darkness, for they will be many; everything that is coming is futility.
verses.11:9: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk blameless in the ways, and not in the sight of your eyes; and know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
verses.11:10: And remove anger from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh, for youth and folly are futility.
verses.12:1: And remember the One who created you in the days of your youth, before the days of trouble come and years arrive in which you will say, "There is no delight for me in them";
verses.12:2: before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars become dark, and the clouds return following the rain;
verses.12:3: in the day when the guards of the house are shaken, and the men of strength are bent, and the grinding women cease because they have grown few, and those who look through the openings will grow dark;
verses.12:4: and they will shut the doors in the marketplace in the weakness of the sound of the grinding woman, and one will rise up at the sound of the sparrow, and all the daughters of song will be brought low,
verses.12:5: and they will look to the height, and terrors will be in the road; and the almond tree will blossom, and the locust will grow fat, and the caperberry will be scattered, because man has gone to his eternal home, and the mourners have gone around in the marketplace;
verses.12:6: before the cord of silver is overturned, and the floral ornament of gold is shattered, and a pitcher is shattered at the spring, and the wheel rolls down into the cistern;
verses.12:7: and the dust returns to the earth just as it was, and the spirit returns to the God who gave it.
verses.12:8: "Futility of futilities," said the Assembler, "all things are futility."
verses.12:9: And moreover, because the Assembler became wise, because he taught knowledge to mankind, an ear will also trace out the adornment of parables.
verses.12:10: The Assembler sought much to find words of delight, and what is written of uprightness, words of truth.
verses.12:11: The words of the wise are like oxgoads and like planted nails, those from the collections; they were given from one shepherd,
verses.12:12: and more than these. My son, beware of making many books; there is no end, and much study is weariness of the flesh.
verses.12:13: The end of the matter, hear it all: Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole man.
verses.12:14: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every overlooked thing, whether good or evil.

notes.1:1: "The Assembler" translates Greek Ekklesiastes ("one who convenes or addresses an assembly").
notes.1:6: In the Greek text, "rising there" opens v. 6 and continues describing the sun's circuit before turning to the wind; in v. 5, "draws" renders Greek helkei (compare MT "pants/hastens").
notes.1:14: Greek proairesis pneumatos ("choice of spirit," also in 1:17; 2:11, 17, 26) reflects taking the Hebrew phrase as "desire/will of spirit" rather than "chasing after wind." Here and in 2:17; 3:10, 17, Greek syn with the accusative functions as a Hebraizing direct-object marker rather than the preposition "with."
notes.1:17: Greek reads "parables and understanding" (parabolas kai epistemen) where the Hebrew MT reads "madness and folly"; likewise in v. 18 Greek reads "abundance of knowledge" (plethos gnoseos, vs. MT "much vexation").
notes.2:3: Greek reads "like wine" (hos oinon, vs. MT "with wine") and "gladness" (euphrosyne, vs. MT "folly").
notes.2:8: Greek renders the obscure Hebrew phrase shiddah weshiddot as "a male cupbearer and female cupbearers" (oinochoon kai oinochoas).
notes.2:12: Greek reads "the counsel" (tes boules, reflecting the Aramaic sense of the root for "king"); the closing clause ta hosa epoiesen auten ("all the things that he did to it") is syntactically compressed and difficult.
notes.2:15: The closing clause "because the fool speaks out of excess" is a distinctive Greek reading absent from the Hebrew MT, explaining the preceding words "I spoke excessively in my heart."
notes.2:22: Greek reads a declarative statement ("For it happens to man...") rather than the Hebrew rhetorical question ("For what does a man have...?"). In v. 24, Greek (like the unemended Hebrew) lacks "except/better"; in v. 25 Greek reads "drink apart from Him" vs. MT "have enjoyment apart from me."
notes.3:11: Greek sympanta ton aiona literally means "all eternity" or "the whole age," adding "all" compared to the Hebrew MT; "in its season" (en kairo autou) could also be read "in His season."
notes.3:15: Greek ton diokomenon is masculine singular ("the one who is pursued" or "persecuted"), rather than neuter ("what has passed away").
notes.3:16: Greek reads "there was the godly one" (ho eusebes) in the second clause, contrasting with "the ungodly one" (ho asebes) in the first, whereas the Hebrew MT has "wickedness" in both places.
notes.3:19: Greek opens with a rhetorical question ("And indeed for them, is there not...?") and answers with "Nothing" (ouden); Greek pneuma here and in v. 21 can mean either "spirit" or "breath."
notes.4:3: The Greek includes the preposition σὺν before πᾶν τὸ ποίημα ("all the evil work"), an ultra-literal rendering of the Hebrew direct-object marker characteristic of Septuagint Ecclesiastes.
notes.4:4: Greek ἀνδρεία literally means "manliness," "vigor," or "prowess" (used in Septuagint Ecclesiastes for skill or capability), and προαίρεσις πνεύματος literally means "choice" or "preference of spirit," rather than "striving after wind."
notes.4:12: Greek ἐπικραταιωθῇ is a middle/passive verb meaning "prevails" or "grows strong," making "one" the assailant against whom "the two will stand."
notes.4:17: Unlike the Hebrew (5:1), the Greek divides the clause so that "your sacrifice" is better than "the gift of fools," and ends literally "they are not knowing of doing evil."
notes.5:5: The Greek reads "before the face of God" where the Hebrew reads "before the messenger," and ἄγνοια denotes an unwitting error or oversight.
notes.5:6: The opening clause in Greek is elliptical, placing "dreams," "futilities," and "many words" all in the genitive governed by "in an abundance of."
notes.5:9: Unlike the Hebrew negative statement, the Greek turns the second clause into a question without a negative ("and who has loved yield in their abundance?").
notes.5:10: The Greek reads ἀρχή ("a beginning," likely an early scribal variant from ἀλλ᾽ ἤ "except") and uses the literal idiom τῷ παρ᾽ αὐτῆς ("the one beside it") to mean "its owner" (similarly in 5:12).
notes.5:19: The Greek reads οὐκ ἄλλα ("not other things"), a distinctive Septuagint reading corresponding to "not much" (οὐ πολλά) in other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew.
notes.6:1: The Greek reads ὑπὸ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ("under mankind"), whereas the Hebrew and some Greek witnesses read "upon mankind."
notes.6:6: Greek καθόδους literally means "descents" or "returns" (rendered here "cycles," where the Hebrew has "twice"), and the final verb πορεύεται is singular without "all."
notes.6:8: Unlike the Hebrew's two rhetorical questions referring to "the living," the Greek forms a declarative statement ("For there is an advantage... because...") and uses the singular "life" (τῆς ζωῆς).
notes.6:12: The opening question belongs to verse 11 in the Hebrew numbering, and Greek ἐποίησεν αὐτὰ ἐν σκιᾷ means "he spent [literally made] them in a shadow" (where the Hebrew reads "like a shadow").
notes.7:3: Greek uses "anger" (matching 7:9) and "badness of face" (a literal rendering of the Hebrew idiom for a sad countenance), and omits the noun "heart" found in the Hebrew text before "will be made good."
notes.7:7: Greek reads "the heart of his nobility" as the object of "destroys," diverging from the Hebrew text ("a bribe destroys the heart").
notes.7:18: Greek reads "do not defile your hand" rather than the Hebrew "do not withdraw your hand," and makes "all things" the subject of "will come forth" for those who fear God.
notes.7:22: Greek diverges markedly from the Hebrew ("your heart knows that many times you yourself have cursed others"), stating instead that the servant will often treat you wickedly and afflict your heart.
notes.7:29: Greek marks the direct object "man" with the preposition syn ("with"), a mechanical rendering of the Hebrew direct-object particle also seen in 7:26, 8:8, 8:15, 8:17, and 9:15. Following Septuagint versification, the closing two questions belong to 7:29 rather than 8:1, with Greek reading "Who knows the wise?" (plural) instead of Hebrew "Who is like the wise man?"
notes.8:1: Greek reads "one shameless in his face will be hated," reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew verb than the Masoretic "the hardness of his face is changed."
notes.8:6: Greek reads "knowledge" (gnosis), reflecting a consonant difference from the Hebrew Masoretic reading "evil" or "trouble."
notes.8:10: Greek reads "were praised" rather than the Hebrew Masoretic "were forgotten."
notes.8:12: Greek reads "from then on and from their long duration" where the Hebrew reads "a hundred times and prolongs his life."
notes.8:17: Following Septuagint versification, the final sentence belongs to 8:17 rather than 9:1, and Greek reads "with my heart I saw all of this" instead of the Hebrew "to examine all of this."
notes.9:2: Greek opens with "futility in all things" (where Hebrew reads "all is the same to all") and includes "and for the bad" after "for the good."
notes.9:9: Greek shifts from "futility" (mataiotes) to "vapor" (atmos) in the nominative clause "All are days of your vapor," rendering two occurrences of the same Hebrew word (hevel) with distinct Greek terms.
notes.9:14: In verses 14-15, Greek uses aorist subjunctive verbs ("may come ... surround ... build ... find ... deliver") for the hypothetical scenario before shifting to the indicative "remembered" at the end of 9:15.
notes.9:17: Greek uses the plurals "rulers" and "in follies" rather than the Hebrew "a ruler among fools."
notes.10:1: The Greek reads active "deadly flies" (where the Hebrew has "dead flies") and "the word of wisdom is more precious than the glory of great foolishness," following the textual reading ho logos ("the word") rather than oligon ("a little") and reversing the sense of the Hebrew text.
notes.10:10: The Greek diverges sharply from the Hebrew, reading "he has troubled the face" and the manuscript reading "the advantage for the man is not wisdom" (to andri ou sophia, contrasting with the variant tou andreiou sophia, "the advantage of the courageous man is wisdom").
notes.10:17: The Greek reads "will not be put to shame" (ouk aischynthesontai), differing from the Hebrew text's "not for drunkenness."
notes.10:19: The Greek adds "and oil" and combines two senses of the underlying Hebrew verb in "will answer to the humbling of money" (tou argyriou tapeinosei epakousetai), which can also be construed as "in humility all things will obey money."
notes.11:5: The Greek begins with third-person "there is no one who knows" (rather than second-person "you do not know") and uses pneuma, which can mean either "spirit" or "wind."
notes.11:7: The Greek idiom syn with the accusative (syn ton helion, also in 12:9) reflects an ultra-literal rendering of the Hebrew direct-object marker rather than the preposition "with."
notes.11:9: The Greek text omits "of your heart," adds "blameless," and inserts the negative "and not" before "in the sight of your eyes," differing markedly from the Hebrew text.
notes.11:10: The Greek reads "folly" (anoia, literally senselessness) where the Hebrew text refers to dark hair or the prime of youth.
notes.12:5: The Greek reads "they will look to the height" (opsontai) where the Hebrew has "they will be afraid of a height," and names the caperberry (kapparis), associated in antiquity with appetite or desire.
notes.12:6: The Greek uses distinctive imagery here: "is overturned" (anatrape), "floral ornament of gold" (anthemion, where the Hebrew has "bowl"), and "rolls down" (syntrochase, a rare compound forming a wordplay on trochos, "wheel").
notes.12:9: The Assembler (Greek ekklesiastes, "one who speaks in an assembly") is followed by a repeated "because" (hoti, shifted from eti, "still/also"), "mankind" rather than "the people," and "an ear will also trace out the adornment of parables," where the Greek construes underlying Hebrew verbs as nouns.
notes.12:12: Following the Greek punctuation, "and more than these" concludes v. 11 and "beware" governs "making many books," whereas the Hebrew connects "beyond these" to "my son, be warned."
notes.12:13: The Greek uses an imperative, "hear it all" (akoue), where the Hebrew has passive "all has been heard," and concludes literally with "this is the whole man" (pas ho anthropos).
